feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: Hackers expose the identities of more than 40,000 DHS employees
entry.summary: A group of hacktivists calling themselves Distributed Denial of Secrets, said the unmasking of ICE agents, DHS operatives and contractors was fair play, given the government's lack of transparency.

entry.title: Judge denies the Justice Department's bid to stop processing California ballots
entry.summary: While the judge rejected the Department of Justice's unprecedented demand in California, the case isn't over yet. The federal government immediately filed notice that it will appeal.

entry.title: A breakthrough for the group on the trail of Chinese hackers
entry.summary: Chinese government hackers are secretly burrowing into critical networks using creative new methods.

entry.title: Israel's election too close to call. And, the Ebola outbreak reaches grim milestone
entry.summary: Israeli voters turned out in record numbers, and the results remain too close to call. And, more than 10,000 people have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak was first declared in May.

entry.title: How a lifelong Republican came to lead the data center battle in Ohio
entry.summary: In Ohio, many people are displeased with the state's rapid buildout of data centers. It's a hot issue in the midterms, as political candidates from both parties try to ease voter concerns.

entry.title: Why many student voters have a right to choose where to register to vote
entry.summary: Student voters studying outside their hometown have a right to choose where they register to vote. Advocates say a Montana legal fight is a reminder of a misunderstanding of those students' rights.

entry.title: Here's how Democrats in Congress are preparing for election fraud claims
entry.summary: Congressional Democrats are working with good governance groups to create an action plan for any potential claims of election fraud.

entry.title: Senate candidates built up massive campaign war chests with out-of-state donations
entry.summary: In several competitive U.S. Senate contests, candidates have built healthy campaign accounts with out-of-state donations. But the messages to those donors is very different from the one back at home.

entry.title: Minnesota becomes battleground as political clashes shape Senate race
entry.summary: Minnesota has become a flashpoint in the political dispute between President Trump and Democrats. Clashes over immigration and recent accusations of fraud are spilling into the U.S. Senate race.

entry.title: A judge halted D.C. golf course renovations. Trump says they'll still start next month
entry.summary: A federal judge has barred the government from clearing more trees or making other alterations to D.C.'s East Potomac Park without proper notice. Trump says his administration will appeal.
